summaryZh: Chavez 研究团队发展操控真核基因组和高通量研究生物现象的遗传工程及合成生物学方法，并将其用于神经生物学与感染性疾病问题。方法包括寡核苷酸芯片合成、文库筛选、iPS 细胞分化和活细胞成像。

evidence.quote: About the lab: Our work employs a variety of techniques ranging from oligo chip synthesis and library-based screening to iPS cell differentiation and live-cell imaging. We utilize a variety of model systems ranging from yeast to human cell culture to assure that the technologies we generate are applicable to a broad swath of the scientific community. Our research group strives to push the boundaries of genetic engineering and synthetic biology by developing methods with which to manipulate eukaryotic genomes and probe biological phenomena in high-throughput. We apply these tools ourselves or through collaboration with a particular focus towards understanding neurobiology and infectious disease. Our team places a strong emphasis on mentoring , and values the opportunity to be able to train the next generation of budding scientists. Lab news: August 2026: This summer a few of our students took their candidacy exams. Congrats to Reema, Gianna, and Andrea all doing super well on their candidacy exams and making it look easy! June 2026: Fun collaborative paper with the Ideker and Krogan labs to rapidly build cell maps was recently published in Cell Reports Methods . Congrats to Scarlett (Ideker lab), Joonwon, and Richa (Krogan lab) on the great work! April 2026: Maddie is awarded an incredibly competitive NSF Graduate Research Fellowship grant. An awesome accomplishment to start off her PhD journey in the lab. March 2026: Shout out to some of our alumni and their amazing accomplishments. Joonwon just got his first big grant as an independent PI and Bruce matched to the University of Washington for Clinical Pathology! So excited to see everyone going out there and being awesome! March 2026: Maddie Wing an amazing BMS PhD student joins the lab! Maddie will be helping lead some of the in vivo CRISPR screening work. March 2026: Lab gets a grant to support efforts around engineering safer AAV vectors. Excited to apply our OptiProt engineering pipeline to an unmet clinical need. September 2025: Bella got the first place prize at the BMS retreat for her research talk. She also got the first place poster prize at the Genetic retreat. We are so proud of her great work, she’s on a roll! September 2025: We’ve had a few nice papers accepted over the past couple months (2 in Nat Comms and 1 in the Journal of Neuroinflammation). Congrats to all the amazing lab members and their hard work getting the work across the finish line! March 2025: Members of the lab applying to PhD or MD, PhD programs all found amazing positions at University of Wisconsin, Rice, and University of Washington. Really proud of how well the group did despite how competitive the application process was this year. Congrats everyone! March 2025: Benji passes his candidacy to PhD exam (as if there was ever a doubt :-)). January 2025: Joonwon K. leaves the lab to start his faculty position at Seoul National University. Joonwon will be missed and we wish him the best of luck in running an awesome research team. December 2024: Visiting undergraduate researcher Randy Tang rounds up his visit in the lab. Good luck Randy on graduate school applications! December 2024: Alex K. and Bruce defend their thesis. The lab won’t be the same without them and we are all truly excited to see the amazing things they accomplish in their careers. December 2024: Debbie’s paper on multiplexed drug screening is accepted to Molecular Systems Biology! October 2024: Marley gives an awesome thesis defense on her work engineering new CRISPR activators. August 2024: Andrea Pence a jointly advised PharmD, PhD student joins the lab! She’ll be working with the protease engineering group to evolve proteases against new disease relevant targets.
